title: What topology hold-out removes—and what it does not

creators.name: Wang, Tao
creators.affiliation: College of Chemical Engineering, Nanjing Tech University, Nanjing 211816, China

description:
Support-audit toolkit and full analysis pipeline for "What topology hold-out removes — and what it does not".

Contents: the v6 manuscript and supplementary information (manuscript_v6/01_manuscript, 02_supplementary), the complete analysis pipeline (scripts/), derived result tables (outputs/), and publication figures (figures_pub/). The repository root also retains the original (v5) reproduction package, so that every path cited in the preceding Zenodo release remains valid in this archive.

Central results: 74.7% of coarse-grained chemical compositions in hMOF occur in a single topology (61.3% of structures); a chemistry-key hold-out produces only 21.1% of the topology hold-out's R2 decrease; on the one usable chemistry-matched pair (pcu <-> nbo) removing the partner topology raised nbo-side MAE by 70.0% while a size-matched control did not; across five independently redrawn 25,000-sample support sets the top-1% hit rate fell from 50.4% to 19.3% under topology-grouped validation (paired difference 31.1 percentage points, 95% interval 24.6-37.6).

The v1.4 deposit adds the six follow-up experiments (outputs/followup_20261023/), the finish analyses (outputs/finish_20261023/), the max_features=1.0 sensitivity (outputs/sensitivity_mf1/) and the paired-seed tests (outputs/paired_tests_20261024.csv); it is the version of record for every analysis in the manuscript. The earlier v1.3 release (10.5281/zenodo.23434268) covers the original analyses only.

The repository was created under an earlier working title that read the topology penalty as "largely" a chemistry penalty. That wording predates the findings reported here and is not the claim of the manuscript, which reports the support loss and a descriptive protocol ratio and does not attribute the topology penalty to chemistry.

Input data are not redistributed: hMOF is available at https://archive.materialscloud.org/records/nsp7v-2dk91 and ARC-MOF v6 at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.13891643. See DATA.md for the retrieval commands and checksums. See REPRODUCE.md for the verification commands (scripts/make_md5sums.py --check, scripts/singleton_audit.py verify).
